Pet Store · Standard

Alert Limit: 8 · Loot: Prize · For: any session that wants guaranteed disaster

The Objective

A specific cricket — yes, a cricket — in the feeder bin behind the service counter. A client is paying in premium silk. Don't ask.

What the Crew Sees at the Score

A three-aisle, single-floor retail space. In plain sight: a large corn snake in a display tank near the counter (its lid is loose, everyone knows, nobody has fixed it), and an alert parrot near the front that repeats what it hears, loudly and at length. Two ways in: the gap in the loading-dock door, or under the front door, right by the parrot.

Present only what's visible. The intel, the threats, and the unknown obstacle are ST information — let Planning reveal the rest.

The pet store. A: the gap in the loading-dock door. B: the gap under the front door. S: the corn snake's tank. P: the parrot's cage. The stockroom floor is cluttered: rough ground. The feeder bin (gold) sits behind the counter; the only way round is the one-square gap by the east wall. The shelves are 6 squares tall. Storyteller's copy: anything dashed in red is the unknown obstacle — keep it off what the crew sees.

One square = one spider. Gold letters are entry points, red tokens are where threats start, numbered circles are the Suggested Obstacles, and E1/E2 lie on the dashed gold escape route.

Intel the crew can uncover by Casing — one true detail per Success, and never more than this list (extra Successes buy nothing; Casing never reveals the unknown obstacle):

  • The snake is slow to commit but fast once it does.
  • The parrot's cage is 5 squares off the main aisle.
  • The feeder bin sits behind the counter with one narrow approach.
  • The parrot's cover is folded on the shelf beside its cage, and there's a box of crackers on the counter.
  • The snake's heat lamp is off for the night.

ST information. Don't foreshadow it in the Score — let it arrive.

There are forty-seven crickets in that bin. The client described the target as “the big one.” They are all the same size. This becomes a negotiation with a cricket. The crickets decide as a group: win them over and they push one forward. It is the big one. Nobody can prove otherwise.

Obstacles 1–4 are the heist: each takes two successful rolls (Partial or better). E1 and E2 are the suggested Escape obstacles: one successful roll each, and at least one of them never needs Athletics. Difficulties are for a calm location; the Alert raises them. Opposed means the creature rolls first, and its Successes + 1 are your Difficulty.

#ObstacleRoll (Difficulty)
1Enter through the loading dock — a gap in the back, but the feeder insects live there and some have opinions.Squeeze the gap, watched: Acrobatics (2) · hush the insects: Persuasion or Intimidation (2), or they chirp: +1 Alert
2Cross the floor past the snake tank. The lid is loose. The snake is aware of you: active from the start.Stealth, opposed (its Perception 3), within 3 squares of the tank · its Weakness — shut the heavy lid properly, or reach the heat lamp's switch over the snake: Engineering (4)
3The parrot. It has seen you. It will describe you. In detail. At volume.A cracker: Persuasion (1) · drop the cover over the cage: Acrobatics (2) · sneak by: Stealth, opposed (its Perception 4)
4(Unknown) Forty-seven identical crickets. Identify the right one. It's a social encounter now.Persuasion or Deception (3) · Intimidation (3), and they all chirp: +1 Alert
E1Back past the tank, carrying a live cricket.Stealth, opposed (the snake) · along the shelf tops: Acrobatics (2), +1 for the height
E2The cricket wants to go home. It will not stop chirping.Calm it: Persuasion (2) · a gentle silk muffle: Engineering (2) · just run: Athletics (3), and it chirps: +1 Alert
